exposure: surgical procedures other than hysterectomy (hypogastric artery ligation and/or B-Lynch suture)
outcome: post-partum depression (measured by Edinburgh Post-natal Depression Scale)
cohort: The study comprised 41 patients, divided into a hysterectomy group and a non-hysterectomy group (those who had experienced surgical procedures other than hysterectomy).
finding: Peripartum hysterectomy was associated with higher Edinburgh Post-natal Depression Scale scores and increased rates of intensive care stay, infant death, and complications, with organ loss significantly increasing the risk of depression.
